key_insight: Kolmogorov-Chapman Maps learn SDE transition distributions without simulated training trajectories, enabling neural sampling across long time intervals.
engineering_relevance: KC-Maps can reduce the GPU cost of molecular simulation by replacing many sequential integration steps with a neural network forward pass.
method: Train using trajectory-free marginal samples and known drift and diffusion coefficients.
Build boundary conditions directly into the neural network architecture.
Use the Kolmogorov–Chapman equation as a training objective to enforce consistent transition dynamics.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful learning of peptide molecular dynamics and lower GPU-hour costs than classical molecular dynamics, without quantified speedups.
watch_item: The method requires marginal samples and known SDE coefficients; the abstract does not establish accuracy or efficiency across broader molecular systems.
paper_title: Kolmogorov-Chapman Maps: Trajectory-Free Learning for Simulating Molecular Dynamics
